_readme: Stamp duty, registration charges and the names of the documents themselves
differ in every state — a 7/12 extract in Maharashtra, an RTC in Karnataka,
a khatauni in UP. Every rule seeds unverified and every fee is an estimate.
Property transactions carry real financial risk: this is a preparation aid,
not legal advice, and the disclaimer on every checklist says so.

documents.name: Sale Deed
documents.description: The registered instrument transferring ownership of the property.

documents.name: Title Deed / Mother Deed
documents.description: The chain of earlier deeds establishing how the seller came to own the property.
documents.notes: The single most important thing to examine before buying. Have it read by a lawyer, not by a checklist.

documents.name: Encumbrance Certificate
documents.description: A statement of registered transactions against a property, showing whether it is mortgaged or disputed.
documents.validityWindow: Usually requested for the last 13 to 30 years

documents.name: Property Card / Khata Extract
documents.description: The municipal record of who holds the property — called a khata, index-2 or property card depending on the state.

documents.name: Stamp Duty Payment Receipt
documents.description: Proof that stamp duty and registration fees have been paid, usually via e-stamping.

documents.name: Society or Builder NOC
documents.description: No-objection letter from the housing society or builder, confirming dues are clear.

documents.name: Approved Building Plan
documents.description: The sanctioned plan and occupancy or completion certificate from the local authority.

services.label: Property Registration
services.description: Register a sale deed and have the transfer recorded at the sub-registrar's office.

questions.label: Is a home loan involved?
questions.helpText: The lender's representative usually attends the registration.

services.label: Property Mutation
services.description: Update the municipal or revenue record so the property stands in your name after a purchase or inheritance.

services.label: Encumbrance Certificate
services.description: Obtain the record of registered transactions against a property before buying it or raising a loan.

services.label: Property Tax
services.description: Get a new property assessed for tax, or change the name the bill is issued in.

actions.label: Change the name on the bill

processSteps.title: Verify the title and get an encumbrance certificate
processSteps.detail: Do this before paying an advance, not after. It is the step that prevents the expensive mistakes.

processSteps.title: Pay stamp duty and registration fees
processSteps.detail: Usually via e-stamping, before the appointment.
processSteps.fee: Stamp duty is a percentage of the property value and differs in every state — commonly 4–7%, with a concession for women buyers in several states

processSteps.title: Deduct and deposit TDS
processSteps.detail: Applies above the statutory transaction value.

processSteps.title: Both parties attend the sub-registrar with the witnesses
Apply for mutation
processSteps.detail: Registration transfers ownership; mutation updates the municipal record. Both are needed.

baseDocuments.note: Showing no arrears — mutation is refused while tax is outstanding.
On stamp paper, and an indemnity bond in many municipalities.

Public notice and objection period

A copy of an earlier deed helps the office locate the right record.

processSteps.title: Apply at the sub-registrar's office or state portal
processSteps.detail: Name the period you want searched — most buyers ask for 13 to 30 years.
